newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha little changed, contango widens.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha little changed, contango widens.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were mostly immobile in slim talks on Thursday with most Asian markets closed for the Labour Day holiday, traders said.
Regional trade is expected to pick up next Tuesday after the three-day weekend in Japan, they said. Japan's oil product market will be closed on Monday for a national holiday.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half July was notionally assessed at around $208.75/209.75 per tonne. The contract was traded at $209.00 in late Wednesday trade.
Second-half July was quoted about 75 cents higher than the first half of the month.
The one-month spread from second-half June was assessed at around minus $3.50/minus $2.50 after switching hands at minus $3.00 on Wednesday.
The contango in near-term spreads widened for the second consecutive day amid ample prompt supplies.
In term talks, Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) and its naphtha lifters will hold term negotiations from June 9 in London on one-year supply contracts starting in August, traders said.
KPC's naphtha premium for one-year contracts which started August 1996 is $7.90 per tonne, and $13.50 for contracts that started in March 1997.--Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
